sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%隐形”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Over the past month, we've all had to make some adjustments to try to stop the spread of COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一个月里，我们所有人都不得不做一些调整，以试图阻止新冠病毒的传播。

sentences.en: Some of them have been small, like me recording this episode underneath a comforter in my bedroom
sentences.zh: 其中一些调整很小，比如我在卧室里的一条厚棉被下录制这一集

sentences.en: instead of in our studio in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 而不是在我们位于美丽的加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心的录音室里。

sentences.en: I mean, that experience is unique to me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种经历对我来说是独一无二的。

sentences.en: But another adjustment that I've made, and one that you probably had to make too,
sentences.zh: 但我做出的另一个调整，也是你可能也不得不去做的一个调整，

sentences.en: is wearing a mask in public.
sentences.zh: 就是在公共场合戴口罩。

sentences.en: And if you've been paying attention to the directives about where and when or even who should be wearing masks,
sentences.zh: 如果你一直关注关于在哪里、何时甚至谁应该戴口罩的指令，

sentences.en: then there's a good chance you've been a little confused, because they've changed dramatically.
sentences.zh: 那么你很有可能会感到有些困惑，因为它们发生了巨大的变化。

sentences.en: Here in the U.S., we're just not used to needing to cover half of our faces in public.
sentences.zh: 在美国这里，我们就是不习惯在公共场合遮住半张脸。

sentences.en: But if you look at the other side of the world, it's a different story.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看世界的另一端，情况就完全不同了。

sentences.en: In parts of Asia, wearing a mask in response to the coronavirus pandemic was a totally easy and normal adjustment.
sentences.zh: 在亚洲的部分地区，为应对冠状病毒大流行而戴口罩是一个完全轻松且正常的调整。

sentences.en: Rebecca Kanther is a reporter based in Shanghai who has lived in China for the past 17 years.
sentences.zh: 丽贝卡·坎瑟是一位驻上海的记者，她在中国生活了过去17年。

sentences.en: And she is here to tell us why the culture of masks developed so differently there,
sentences.zh: 她今天在这里向我们讲述为什么那里的口罩文化发展得如此不同，

sentences.en: and the doctor who started it all.
sentences.zh: 以及开启这一切的那位医生。

sentences.en: Yeah, I remember the first time I really started taking this seriously.
sentences.zh: 是的，我记得我真正开始认真对待这件事的第一天。

sentences.en: I was traveling on my way home to see my in-laws, actually, for Chinese New Year.
sentences.zh: 其实我当时正踏上回家看望公公婆婆的旅程，正值中国新年。

sentences.en: And the night before, I'd gone out.
sentences.zh: 就在前一天晚上，我还出门了。

sentences.en: Everything was normal.
sentences.zh: 一切都很正常。

sentences.en: And then that morning, I walked out the door, and, you know, I put the location on my GPS app on my phone.
sentences.zh: 然后那天早上，我走出门，你知道的，我在手机的GPS应用上设置了位置。

sentences.en: And you know how, on your phone, you know, the GPS app will tell you in this, like, nice, calm voice, you know, which direction to start off in?
sentences.zh: 你知道在手机上，GPS应用通常会用那种好听、平静的声音告诉你该从哪个方向出发，对吧？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对的。

sentences.en: Well, this time, my GPS app said this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这次我的GPS应用是这么说的。

sentences.en: 準備出发.
sentences.zh: 准备出发。

sentences.en: 高德提醒您注意疫情防護.
sentences.zh: 高德提醒您注意疫情防护。

sentences.en: 戴好口罩.
sentences.zh: 戴好口罩。

sentences.en: 请注意安全.
sentences.zh: 请注意安全。

sentences.en: So it's saying, please wear a mask if you're going out.
sentences.zh: 所以它是在说，如果你要出门，请戴上口罩。

sentences.en: Be safe.
sentences.zh: 注意安全。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I don't think my GPS has ever been quite that intimate with me before.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我的GPS以前从来没有对我这么亲密过。

sentences.en: Yeah, my phone's never gotten that personal with me before.
sentences.zh: 对啊，我的手机以前从来没有对我这么私人过。

sentences.en: I mean, it's, like, totally weird.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直太诡异了。

sentences.en: So it stuck with me.
sentences.zh: 所以这件事让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: And then, you know, after I heard that, then I, you know, I was looking around, and I started noticing everyone around me on the street was wearing a mask.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，在我听到这个之后，我环顾四周，开始注意到街上的每个人都戴着口罩。

sentences.en: It was like, between the day before and that day, like, a switch had been flipped.
sentences.zh: 就好像在前一天和那天之间，有人按下了开关一样。

sentences.en: Everyone knew exactly what to do.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道该做什么。

sentences.en: So a week later, I got back to Shanghai, and the change was just even more drastic.
sentences.zh: 所以一周后，我回到上海，这种变化甚至更加剧烈。

sentences.en: You know, people weren't going outside, but anyone who did go outside was wearing a mask.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，人们都不出门，但任何出门的人都戴着口罩。

sentences.en: And there were posters all over reminding people to wear masks.
sentences.zh: 到处都是提醒人们戴口罩的海报。

sentences.en: And I was riding my bike one day, and I passed this loudspeaker with a voice that was just, like, on a loop, reminding people to wear a mask.
sentences.zh: 有一天我骑着自行车，经过一个大喇叭，里面循环播放着提醒人们戴口罩的声音。

sentences.en: And so the thing is, like, everyone has to wear a mask.
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，每个人都得戴口罩。

sentences.en: But at that time, you couldn't buy one anywhere.
sentences.zh: 但在那个时候，你根本买不到。

sentences.en: Like, the pharmacies were all sold out.
sentences.zh: 药店里的口罩都卖光了。

sentences.en: I mean, I tried online.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我在网上也试过了。

sentences.en: So does that mean that everyone just already had a mask?
sentences.zh: 那是不是意味着每个人本来就都有口罩？

sentences.en: Yeah, I guess.
sentences.zh: 对，我猜是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, I think people had masks at home.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想大家家里都有口罩。

sentences.en: So, I mean, eventually, a friend gave me some, which was really nice.
sentences.zh: 所以，最终一个朋友给了我一些，这真的很好。

sentences.en: But the whole experience got me wondering, like, how come everybody else was so prepared?
sentences.zh: 但整个经历让我纳闷，为什么其他人准备得这么充分？

sentences.en: And I'm, like, the only idiot, like, got caught off guard.
sentences.zh: 而我却像个唯一措手不及的笨蛋。

sentences.en: I mean, right.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: I mean, it seems like, I mean, you're from the U.S., and, you know, I'm here in the U.S., and we just seem to have a very different relationship with masks in general.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来，你是美国人，你知道的，我在美国，我们对口罩的整体态度似乎有很大不同。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it's, like, nothing that I counted as something I should keep in my first aid kit at home.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，这根本不是我认为应该放在家里急救箱里的东西。

sentences.en: But I guess everyone else here was doing that.
sentences.zh: 但我猜这里的其他人都在这么做。

sentences.en: And so why do you think that is?
sentences.zh: 那你觉得这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Why does China have a different relationship with masks?
sentences.zh: 为什么中国对口罩的态度如此不同？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I was really curious about that.
sentences.zh: 对，其实我对此也十分好奇。

sentences.en: So I started looking into the history of masks in China.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始研究中国口罩的历史。

sentences.en: And it turns out they've been used here for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 结果发现它们在这里已经使用了很长时间。

sentences.en: So, Roman, I sent you a photo in the Zoom chat.
sentences.zh: 所以，罗曼，我在Zoom聊天里给你发了一张照片。

sentences.en: Do you have it there?
sentences.zh: 你看到了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 看到了。

sentences.en: So this is a black and white photo.
sentences.zh: 这是一张黑白照片。

sentences.en: It's a couple people wearing, you know, big white masks.
sentences.zh: 有几个人戴着那种很大的白色口罩。

sentences.en: Like, everything is kind of covered except for the eyes.
sentences.zh: 除了眼睛，基本上全身都遮住了。

sentences.en: But, and it's, like, a little thicker and gauzier than the ones that we might see people wearing around today.
sentences.zh: 而且它比我们今天看到人们戴的口罩要稍微厚一点，更像纱布。

sentences.en: But it's basically the same principle.
sentences.zh: 但它的基本原理是一样的。

sentences.en: You know, it's a mask.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是个口罩。

sentences.en: So when was this photo taken?
sentences.zh: 那这张照片是什么时候拍的？

sentences.en: So this photo is from over 100 years ago, when China was the scene of another devastating epidemic, the Great Manchurian Plague.
sentences.zh: 这张照片是一百多年前拍的，当时中国正经历另一场毁灭性的流行病——东北鼠疫。

sentences.en: Oh, wow, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇，好吧。

sentences.en: Manchurian, at the time, was contested territory.
sentences.zh: 当时的满洲是争议领土。

sentences.en: It's where northeast China is today.
sentences.zh: 也就是今天的中国东北。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in 1910, it became the site of a really deadly outbreak of plague.
sentences.zh: 在1910年，这里爆发了一场非常致命的鼠疫。

sentences.en: 95% or more of those that got infected died.
sentences.zh: 95%或更多的感染者都死亡了。

sentences.en: And they died fast, within just a few days of contracting the virus.
sentences.zh: 而且他们死得很快，在感染病毒后几天内就去世了。

sentences.en: And this outbreak was really well documented, especially in photographs.
sentences.zh: 这次疫情有很好的记录，特别是通过照片。

sentences.en: It was the first time that you had cameras that could readily cover an epidemic.
sentences.zh: 那是第一次有相机能够方便地记录疫情。

sentences.en: But also it was the first time that newspapers could carry these images, you know, could carry good quality photographic images.
sentences.zh: 这也是第一次报纸能够刊登这些图像，你知道的，刊登高质量的摄影图像。

sentences.en: So this is Christos Linteres.
sentences.zh: 这位是克里斯托斯·林特雷斯。

sentences.en: He's a medical anthropologist at University of St. Andrews in the UK.
sentences.zh: 他是英国圣安德鲁斯大学的医学人类学家。

sentences.en: And he said that at that time, photos of the outbreak in Manchuria were seen in newspapers around the world.
sentences.zh: 他说，在那个时候，满洲疫情的照片在全世界的报纸上都能看到。

sentences.en: And photography played a key role in establishing this idea of a global outbreak, you know, an outbreak which is spreading across the globe.
sentences.zh: 摄影在确立全球疫情这一概念方面发挥了关键作用，也就是正在全球蔓延的疫情。

sentences.en: So a lot of these photographs were quite graphic scenes of victiMs.
sentences.zh: 所以许多照片都是受害者相当惨烈的场景。

sentences.en: But there were also a lot of photographs of people wearing masks, like the one I showed you.
sentences.zh: 但也有很多人们戴着口罩的照片，就像我给你看的那张一样。

sentences.en: And at the center of this photography is the mask.
sentences.zh: 而这些照片的核心就是口罩。

sentences.en: Now, why the mask?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么要戴口罩？

sentences.en: Masks had been used before for surgery.
sentences.zh: 以前外科手术曾使用过口罩。

sentences.en: So I think the official history of the mask in a clinical setting or on the operation theater dates back from around 1897.
sentences.zh: 我想临床环境或手术室里口罩的官方历史可以追溯到1897年左右。

sentences.en: But masks had never been systematically used in an epidemic before.
sentences.zh: 但在此之前，口罩从未在流行病中被系统地使用过。

sentences.en: So masks had been used by doctors, but they weren't being used by the general public at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以医生们用过口罩，但在当时普通公众并没有使用。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But that changed in Manchuria because of one guy.
sentences.zh: 但这种情况在满洲改变了，因为一个人。

sentences.en: His name was Wu Lian De.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫伍连德。

sentences.en: Dr. Wu was a young Chinese-Malaysian doctor who had gone abroad to study medicine in Europe.
sentences.zh: 伍医生是一位年轻的马来西亚籍华人医生，曾去欧洲学习医学。

sentences.en: And he was actually the first ethnic Chinese person to study at Cambridge.
sentences.zh: 他实际上是第一个在剑桥大学求学的华人。

sentences.en: The Qing Dynasty government called him in to lead the Chinese efforts against the plague, since it was an international effort.
sentences.zh: 清朝政府请他来领导中国的抗鼠疫工作，因为这是一项国际合作。

sentences.en: And he was surrounded by all these much more experienced doctors from Russia, Japan, France, Great Britain.
sentences.zh: 他身边环绕着来自俄罗斯、日本、法国和英国的更有经验的医生。

sentences.en: And he was only in his early 30s, but he was really smart.
sentences.zh: 他当时才三十出头，但非常聪明。

sentences.en: And he was a brilliant scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一位杰出的科学家。

sentences.en: And he soon came across people with symptoms and he concluded, OK, this is a pneumonic plague.
sentences.zh: 他很快遇到了有症状的患者，并得出结论：好的，这是肺鼠疫。

sentences.en: And he had this idea that it spread in an airborne manner.
sentences.zh: 他认为它是通过空气传播的。

sentences.en: So meaning it spread from droplets in the air coming from people's noses or mouths.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它通过人们鼻子或嘴巴产生的空气飞沫传播。

sentences.en: And was this a new idea?
sentences.zh: 这是一个新观点吗？

sentences.en: I mean, how did people think it was being spread at the time?
sentences.zh: 当时人们认为它是怎么传播的？

sentences.en: Well, you know, there's different kinds of plague.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，鼠疫有好几种。

sentences.en: There's bubonic and septicemic.
sentences.zh: 有腺鼠疫和败血症鼠疫。

sentences.en: Those ones are spread by fleas from small animals.
sentences.zh: 那些是通过小型动物身上的跳蚤传播的。

sentences.en: And at the time, most of the experts thought that was how this plague was spreading.
sentences.zh: 当时大多数专家认为这场鼠疫就是这样传播的。

sentences.en: But Dr. Wu, he figured out that this outbreak was a different kind of plague.
sentences.zh: 但伍医生发现这次疫情是一种不同类型的鼠疫。

sentences.en: I mean, he was treating all these people with respiratory symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他当时在治疗所有这些有呼吸道症状的病人。

sentences.en: And he was convinced that the plague bacteria was spreading through the air.
sentences.zh: 他坚信鼠疫杆菌是通过空气传播的。

sentences.en: And he was right about it.
sentences.zh: 事实证明他是对的。

sentences.en: Way to go, Dr. Wu.
sentences.zh: 干得好，伍医生。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so he made us like it seemed like a simple suggestion.
sentences.zh: 所以他提出了一个看似简单的建议。

sentences.en: Everyone should start covering their mouth and noses with face masks.
sentences.zh: 每个人都应该开始用口罩遮住口鼻。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which is the suggestion that we're all getting today to stop the spread of coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们今天为了阻止新冠病毒传播而收到的建议。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But that was the first time someone had suggested that.
sentences.zh: 但这在那时是前所未有的建议。

sentences.en: And he was really serious about this idea.
sentences.zh: 而且他对这个想法非常认真。

sentences.en: He designed face masks himself.
sentences.zh: 他亲自设计了口罩。

sentences.en: And so I talked to this historian at Shanghai Library.
sentences.zh: 所以我采访了上海图书馆的一位历史学家。

sentences.en: Her name's Vivian Huang.
sentences.zh: 她叫黄香。

sentences.en: And she's been researching the history of Wu's mask.
sentences.zh: 她一直在研究伍连德口罩的历史。

sentences.en: And she was telling me about how it was designed.
sentences.zh: 她向我讲述了它是如何被设计的。

sentences.en: She speaks Chinese.
sentences.zh: 她说中文。

sentences.en: So I'm just going to translate what she said.
sentences.zh: 所以我来翻译她的话。

sentences.en: She said it was this basic gauze mask with two layers.
sentences.zh: 她说这是一种两层的基础纱布口罩。

sentences.en: And in between the layers, there was about a four by six inch piece of cotton that was about a half inch thick.
sentences.zh: 在两层之间，有一块大约四乘六英寸、厚度约半英寸的棉花。

sentences.en: And then there were these two strings to tie the mask behind your head.
sentences.zh: 然后有两条带子用来把口罩系在脑后。

sentences.en: And all of these materials were really cheap and easy to find at the time.
sentences.zh: 所有这些材料在当时都非常便宜且容易找到。

sentences.en: And so it was something that was meant to be very simple, very easy and cheap to produce and which he envisioned that all his doctors,
sentences.zh: 所以它旨在非常简单、非常容易且廉价地生产，他设想他所有的医生、

sentences.en: all his nurses and all his sanitary staff should use while engaged in anti-plague operations.
sentences.zh: 所有的护士和所有的卫生人员在进行抗鼠疫工作时都应该使用它。

sentences.en: And he wants the general public to wear these masks as well.
sentences.zh: 他还希望普通公众也佩戴这些口罩。

sentences.en: But the other doctors in Manchuria at the time, they wouldn't listen to him.
sentences.zh: 但当时满洲的其他医生不听他的。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe it was because he was young or maybe because China at that time wasn't really known for its scientific prowess.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许是因为他年轻，或者是因为当时中国在科学实力上并不出名。

sentences.en: They just didn't believe him.
sentences.zh: 他们就是不相信他。

sentences.en: Or maybe it's because they're racists.
sentences.zh: 或者也许是因为他们有种族偏见。

sentences.en: No, but even the local leaders were suspicious of him.
sentences.zh: 不，甚至连当地领导人对他也心存怀疑。

sentences.en: I mean, he was just nobody believed him.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，根本没有人相信他。

sentences.en: And I think it was because he was kind of a nobody compared to all these famous European and Japanese doctors.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为与所有这些著名的欧洲和日本医生相比，他有点无名小卒的意思。

sentences.en: So they antagonized him very, very actively.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对他进行了非常非常积极的敌对。

sentences.en: And there is this incident which he recounts in his autobiography, which is called The Plague Fighter, where he's confronted by a famous French doctor, Gérald Mezny.
sentences.zh: 在他的自传《鼠疫斗士》中记录了这样一件事：他遭到了法国著名医生杰拉尔·梅兹尼的质问。

sentences.en: And Mezny hears Wu expounding his airborne plague theory and he humiliates him in a very racist manner.
sentences.zh: 梅兹尼听到伍连德阐述他的空气传播鼠疫理论时，以非常带有种族歧视的方式羞辱了他。

sentences.en: And then Mezny goes on to operate in one of the hospitals to attend the sick without wearing what Wu had suggested is an essential device, which is the mask.
sentences.zh: 然后梅兹尼继续在其中一家医院进行手术，照顾病人，却没有戴伍连德所建议的必不可少的设备，也就是口罩。

sentences.en: So I think you can guess where this is going.
sentences.zh: 所以我想你大概能猜到接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: Unfortunately for the French doctor, he dies soon after.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，这位法国医生不久后就去世了。

sentences.en: He catches the plague and he dies.
sentences.zh: 他感染了鼠疫，然后去世了。

sentences.en: So Wu is suddenly and completely unexpectedly, for most people, vindicated.
sentences.zh: 所以对大多数人来说，伍连德突然且完全出乎意料地得到了平反。

sentences.en: That is dramatic.
sentences.zh: 这太戏剧性了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, we don't know if the mask would have saved him.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们不知道口罩是不是真的能救他的命。

sentences.en: But after he died, it was just this huge case in point that proved that Wu had been right.
sentences.zh: 但他在死后，这成了一个极具说服力的实例，证明了伍连德是对的。

sentences.en: So the moment when Mezny dies and basically everyone starts accepting Wu's theory, you know, this mask goes viral.
sentences.zh: 所以，在梅兹尼去世的那一刻，基本上所有人都开始接受伍连德的理论，你知道的，这款口罩就这样火了。

sentences.en: I don't know if I'll ever be able to use that phrase quite the same way as I used to, but I get his point.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我以后还能不能像以前那样自然地使用这个词，但我明白他的意思。

sentences.en: At this point, like, it just spreads everywhere.
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，它就像是传遍了每个地方。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it was reported on all over the world.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，全世界都在对此进行报道。

sentences.en: The Manchurian plague ended after seven months.
sentences.zh: 满洲鼠疫在七个月后结束了。

sentences.en: Some people say it ended because spring came and the weather warmed up.
sentences.zh: 有人说它结束是因为春天来了，天气变暖了。

sentences.en: But Dr. Wu claimed victory because of the recommendations he made to stop its spread, wearing masks, quarantining sick patients, cutting off the Trans-Siberian railway lines.
sentences.zh: 但伍博士将功劳归于他为阻止疫情蔓延而提出的建议：戴口罩、隔离病患、切断西伯利亚大铁路。

sentences.en: But Dr. Wu's mask became the symbol for his successfully controlling the outbreak.
sentences.zh: 但伍博士的口罩成了他成功控制疫情的象征。

sentences.en: Everyone wants the mask and everyone starts photographing the mask.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想要这个口罩，每个人都开始拍摄口罩的照片。

sentences.en: And the mask becomes this kind of a symbol of scientific success and medical ability to cope with this dreadful disease in Manchuria.
sentences.zh: 而口罩成了满洲这场可怕疾病中，科学成功和医疗应对能力的一种象征。

sentences.en: And Wu is praised, of course, as a genius in having invented it.
sentences.zh: 当然，伍连德因发明了它而被誉为天才。

sentences.en: So it's a huge success story for Wu.
sentences.zh: 所以对伍连德来说，这是一个巨大的成功故事。

sentences.en: And he came out of this as, you know, the guy who was internationally recognized as having control of the epidemic,
sentences.zh: 他从中脱颖而出，成为了你知道的那个在国际上被公认控制了疫情的人，

sentences.en: which was astonishing because he was a nobody until then.
sentences.zh: 这太令人惊叹了，因为在此之前他只是个无名小卒。

sentences.en: And he was competing with very, very famous doctors.
sentences.zh: 而且他当时在与非常非常著名的医生竞争。

sentences.en: Dr. Wu went on to form China's first organization dealing with disease control.
sentences.zh: 伍博士随后创立了中国第一个处理疾病控制的组织。

sentences.en: And then later he formed the Chinese Medical Association.
sentences.zh: 后来他又成立了中华医学会。

sentences.en: His work is the basis for China's disease control and public health system today.
sentences.zh: 他的工作奠定了今天中国疾病控制和公共卫生系统的基础。

sentences.en: And do people remember him today?
sentences.zh: 那么今天人们还记得他吗？

sentences.en: I mean, did he get the recognition that he deserved?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他得到了应有的认可吗？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, in 1935, he was nominated for a Nobel Prize.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，在1935年，他曾被提名诺贝尔奖。

sentences.en: Well, that's pretty good.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这相当不错。

sentences.en: Yeah, OK.
sentences.zh: 对，好吧。

sentences.en: But today, I mean, he never became a household name, not even in China.
sentences.zh: 但今天，我的意思是，他从未成为一个家喻户晓的名字，甚至在中国也不是。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, people don't know him.
sentences.zh: 我是说，对，人们并不认识他。

sentences.en: But still, you know, he's one of the most significant epidemiologists of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，你知道的，他是20世纪最重要的流行病学家之一。

sentences.en: So it's a shame that he's not better known.
sentences.zh: 所以他没有更大的名气，真是一种遗憾。

sentences.en: So what happens with Wu's mask after the Manchurian plague?
sentences.zh: 那么满洲鼠疫之后，伍连德的口罩怎么样了？

sentences.en: Where does it go?
sentences.zh: 它去哪儿了？

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Wu's design inspired others around the world to try their hand at mask design, too.
sentences.zh: 嗯，伍博士的设计启发了世界各地的其他人，让他们也想尝试设计口罩。

sentences.en: And so there were competing models.
sentences.zh: 因此出现了各种竞争款式。

sentences.en: So it becomes kind of a medical competition and design competition for the best mask.
sentences.zh: 所以这在某种程度上变成了关于最佳口罩的医疗竞争和设计竞争。

sentences.en: You know, it's the holy grail of that epidemic.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就是那场疫情中的圣杯。

sentences.en: You know, who is going to produce the best mask, the most efficient mask?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，谁能生产出最好的口罩、最高效的口罩？

sentences.en: And some of them are really kind of weird things.
sentences.zh: 其中有些东西真的很诡异。

sentences.en: You know, they look like, I don't know, like a diver's suit or something.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它们看起来像，我不知道，就像潜水服之类的。

sentences.en: Others are more simple.
sentences.zh: 其他的则更简单一些。

sentences.en: But Wu's is the one which prevails.
sentences.zh: 但最终胜出的是伍连德设计的口罩。

sentences.en: One of the key things, I think, about Wu's design was that it was disposable.
sentences.zh: 我认为，伍连德设计的一个关键之处在于它是用完即弃的。

sentences.en: So it didn't need to be disinfected.
sentences.zh: 所以它不需要消毒。

sentences.en: Some of the other designs were just too complicated.
sentences.zh: 其他的一些设计实在是太复杂了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这很合理。

sentences.en: So seven years later, when the 1918 flu epidemic hit, masks similar to the ones that Dr. Wu designed
sentences.zh: 因此，七年后的1918年流感爆发时，类似于伍博士设计的口罩

sentences.en: started being used around the world.
sentences.zh: 开始在世界各地被使用。

sentences.en: This was a device that was globally recognized by doctors as well as the public as a necessary
sentences.zh: 这是一种被医生以及公众在全球范围内认可为必要

sentences.en: and efficient anti-contagion device.
sentences.zh: 且高效的抗传染装置。

sentences.en: You know, I don't know, you know, how easy it would have been to make people accept these
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不知道，如果不是因为刚刚经历了一场被

sentences.en: masks, you know, and adopt them if it had not been part of a recent outbreak that had been
sentences.zh: 成功控制的疫情，要让人们接受这些

sentences.en: successfully controlled.
sentences.zh: 口罩并采用它们会有多容易。

sentences.en: And during the 1918 flu, Americans wore masks a lot like Dr. Wu's.
sentences.zh: 在1918年流感期间，美国人戴的口罩和伍博士的很像。

sentences.en: Nancy Toms is a history professor at SUNY Stony Brook, and she's written a lot about the epidemic.
sentences.zh: 南希·托姆斯是纽约州立大学石溪分校的历史学教授，她写过很多关于这场疫情的文章。

sentences.en: She told me about all these great photos of Americans wearing masks during the flu epidemic.
sentences.zh: 她跟我讲了许多流感期间美国人戴口罩的精彩照片。

sentences.en: So there's this really wonderful picture of a baseball game in Pasadena, California.
sentences.zh: 加州帕萨迪纳有一张非常棒的棒球比赛照片。

sentences.en: And you can see the umpire, the catcher, and the pitcher, who's up to bat, all wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到裁判、捕手，以及准备击球的投手，全都戴着口罩。

sentences.en: And then behind them, you can see the spectators also wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 在他们身后，你还能看到观众也戴着口罩。

sentences.en: So if people were wearing them during a baseball game, like I can barely wear one, like, on a brisk walk
sentences.zh: 所以如果人们在棒球比赛时都戴着口罩，而我连在微凉的街道上

sentences.en: for a couple blocks.
sentences.zh: 快走几个街区都快戴不住，

sentences.en: So, like, does this mean that everyone was wearing masks at this point?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是否意味着当时每个人都在戴口罩？

sentences.en: Okay, so to be fair, I think that was the only baseball game where people wore them.
sentences.zh: 好吧，公平地说，我认为那是唯一一场人们戴口罩的棒球比赛。

sentences.en: It was reported as the first baseball game where players wore masks, and it was probably
sentences.zh: 据报道，这是第一场球员戴口罩的棒球比赛，而且可能

sentences.en: also the last one.
sentences.zh: 也是最后一场。

sentences.en: Yeah, so it was a little bit of propaganda to get people to wear masks, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，所以这有点像为了让人们戴口罩而做的宣传，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, it was for show.
sentences.zh: 对，就是做个样子。

sentences.en: Professor Toms said that these photos, they're mostly police officers, nurses, but also baseball
sentences.zh: 托姆斯教授说，这些照片里的人大多是警察、护士，还有棒球

sentences.en: players and society ladies.
sentences.zh: 运动员和名媛贵妇。

sentences.en: They were meant to convince more people to wear masks.
sentences.zh: 它们旨在说服更多人戴口罩。

sentences.en: So they were like Instagram influencers.
sentences.zh: 所以他们就像是Instagram网红。

sentences.en: Totally, totally, yes.
sentences.zh: 完全是，完全是，是的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, this time around, during this pandemic, I've been seeing news items and on social media
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这一次大流行期间，我一直看到新闻和社交媒体上

sentences.en: photos from back in the 1918 pandemic.
sentences.zh: 流传着1918年大流行时期的照片。

sentences.en: And you see these photos, and I guess it's easy to assume that everyone was wearing the mask.
sentences.zh: 当你看到这些照片时，很容易让人以为当时每个人都戴着口罩。

sentences.en: But Professor Toms says we shouldn't assume that it was that universal.
sentences.zh: 但托姆斯教授说，我们不应该认为它那么普及。

sentences.en: It's, I call it an elite practice, but a specialized practice.
sentences.zh: 我称之为精英做法，或者说是一种专业化的做法。

sentences.en: So you're going to find it among certain groups, and their wearing of it is going to be replicated
sentences.zh: 所以你会在某些群体中发现它，而他们佩戴口罩的行为将被复制

sentences.en: as a way to make everybody feel calmer and safer.
sentences.zh: 作为一种让每个人都感到更平静、更安全的方式。

sentences.en: But what's the expectation that every American should go around with a gauze mask?
sentences.zh: 但那种认为每个美国人都应该戴着纱布口罩到处走的期望存在吗？

sentences.en: I don't think that happened.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那并没有发生。

sentences.en: Still, local health officials were calling on people to wear masks.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，当地卫生官员仍在呼吁人们戴口罩。

sentences.en: And in some cities, there were mask ordinances.
sentences.zh: 在某些城市，甚至还有口罩令。

sentences.en: So if you were caught without one, you were fined or you went to jail.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你出门不戴口罩被抓到，就会被罚款或入狱。

sentences.en: And women were being called upon to sew masks for the cause.
sentences.zh: 妇女们也被号召为大局缝制口罩。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Which is another thing you see today.
sentences.zh: 这也是你在今天能看到的另一个现象。

sentences.en: So right after that 1918 pandemic ended, Americans kind of stopped using masks.
sentences.zh: 所以在1918年大流行刚结束时，美国人差不多就不再使用口罩了。

sentences.en: So it was just kind of this like blip in American history where it wasn't unusual to wear a mask.
sentences.zh: 所以它只是美国历史上的一个小插曲，当时戴口罩并不是什么不寻常的事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Masks basically fell into obscurity in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 此后，口罩在美国基本上被人们遗忘了。

sentences.en: after that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，20世纪期间还有其他流行病，但在美国它们不是通过咳嗽和打喷嚏传播的。

sentences.en: I mean, there were other epidemics throughout the 20th century, but they weren't spread by coughing and sneezing in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但在中国，人们从来没有机会把口罩忘掉太久。

sentences.en: But in China, there was never a chance for people to forget masks for too long.
sentences.zh: 首先，在中国，口罩的使用具有连续性，对吧？

sentences.en: First of all, in China, you have a continuity of the use of the mask, right?
sentences.zh: 所以口罩的故事并没有在1911年或1918年结束。

sentences.en: So the mask story does not end in 1911 or 1918.
sentences.zh: 它在20年代和30年代的其他几次疫情中延续了下来。

sentences.en: It continues, you know, through several other outbreaks in the 20s and the 30s.
sentences.zh: 然后在中国毛泽东时代，1949年之后，口罩再次在公共卫生运动中发挥了重要作用。

sentences.en: And then in Maoist China, after 1949, again, the mask plays an important role in public health campaigns.
sentences.zh: 你在大量的公共卫生宣传海报上都能看到口罩。

sentences.en: You see the masks in a great number of public health propaganda posters.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个相当重要的点。

sentences.en: I think this is kind of an important point.
sentences.zh: 许多人会说，在中国戴口罩是一种文化现象。

sentences.en: A lot of folks would say that wearing a mask is kind of a cultural thing in China.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这某种程度上是真的，但黄文娴（Vivian Huang）告诉我，口罩在中国变得习以为常，只是因为国家要求他们佩戴。

sentences.en: I think that's kind of true, but Vivian Huang was telling me that it's only normalized in China because they were required to wear them by the state.
sentences.zh: 黄告诉我，社区黑板报或电线杆上的海报等公共卫生宣传都在推广戴口罩。

sentences.en: Huang told me that public health campaigns on neighborhood chalkboards or posters on telephone poles all promoted wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 在20年代和30年代，上海的报纸发表了文章和漫画，试图普及口罩的使用。

sentences.en: And in the 20s and 30s, Shanghai newspapers, they published articles and cartoons that tried to popularize the use of masks.
sentences.zh: 是的，女性杂志将口罩描绘成一种身份的象征。

sentences.en: Yeah, and women's magazines showed masks as kind of like a status symbol.
sentences.zh: 当时还有杂志文章教读者如何自己织口罩。

sentences.en: And there were these magazine articles teaching readers how to knit their own masks.
sentences.zh: 我也快要赶上这种时尚了，因为我有一种更偏向技术型的买来的口罩，比如从加州野火时留下的N95。

sentences.en: I'm falling for this fashion thing as well because I have a kind of more technical store-bought mask, like an N95 leftover from the wildfires of California.
sentences.zh: 但我也有一个手工制作的口罩，它可能没有工厂制造的那么高效，但我更喜欢戴它，因为它更好看。

sentences.en: But I also have a handmade one, and it might not have the efficacy of the manufactured one, but I like wearing it more because it's prettier.
sentences.zh: 完全正确，完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 就像，你更愿意戴那些你喜欢它外观的东西。

sentences.en: Like, you're more willing to wear something that you like the way it looks.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: Yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，历经这一切，伍博士的纱布口罩设计或与之类似的设计得以保留下来。

sentences.en: Anyway, through it all, Dr. Wu's gauze mask design, or something similar to it, survived.
sentences.zh: 如果我们快进到2002年的SARS疫情，口罩又一次出现了。

sentences.en: And then if we flash forward to the 2002 SARS epidemic, again, masks appeared.
sentences.zh: 医生们戴着医用外科口罩，但黄文娴记得看到街上有人戴着类似于伍博士设计的口罩。

sentences.en: Doctors were wearing surgical masks, but Vivian Huang remembers seeing people on the streets wearing masks similar to the ones that Dr. Wu designed.
sentences.zh: 她回溯说，那时候她还是一名学生。

sentences.en: Back then, she says she was a student.
sentences.zh: 她被困在上海的大学校园里隔离。

sentences.en: She was stuck on lockdown on her university campus in Shanghai.
sentences.zh: 这一次，关于勤洗手和戴口罩的公共卫生运动再次展开。

sentences.en: And once again, there were public health campaigns on handwashing and wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 她说这就是为什么这一次，每个人都记得并且知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: And she says that's why this time around, everyone remembered and knew what to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，这并不完全是因为中国人在文化上更倾向于戴口罩。

sentences.en: So it's not exactly that, you know, people in China are more, like, inclined culturally to wear masks.
sentences.zh: 只是他们在近代史上有更多机会佩戴口罩，所以他们知道该怎么做，也知道这是怎么回事。

sentences.en: They just had more occasion in recent history to wear masks, and so they know what to do, and they know what the deal is.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是说中国人习惯戴口罩一直都很容易。

sentences.en: But that's not to say it's been easy for Chinese people to get used to wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 我是说，即使是这一次，一开始老人们真的很抗拒。

sentences.en: I mean, even this time around, at first, older people really resisted.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 我们这里也差不多是这样。

sentences.en: That kind of happened here, too.
sentences.zh: 我们试图说服我们那一代婴儿潮的父母待在家里，因为我们担心他们会死，你知道的，所以。

sentences.en: We were trying to convince our boomer parents to stay in because we were fearful they would die, you know, so.
sentences.zh: 对，情况是一样的。

sentences.en: Yeah, and it's the same thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这里的年轻人告诉我，一开始他们真的不得不唠叨父母和祖父母戴口罩，

sentences.en: I mean, younger people here were telling me that at first they were really having to nag their parents and grandparents to wear masks,
sentences.zh: 他们开玩笑说，他们唠叨长辈戴口罩的劲头，跟长辈催他们结婚的力度不相上下。

sentences.en: and they were joking that they had to nag their, you know, older relatives with the same intensity that they were being nagged to get married.
sentences.zh: 所以，就是那种直接而坚持不懈的唠叨。

sentences.en: So, like, direct and relentless.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 他们每天给家人打电话说，请戴口罩，请戴口罩。

sentences.en: They're calling up their family every day saying, please wear a mask, please wear a mask.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，黄文娴告诉我，中国人真的花了一百年才走到在传染病爆发期间接受戴口罩这一步。

sentences.en: So, yeah, Vivian Huang told me it's really taken Chinese people a hundred years to get to this point of acceptance of wearing masks during an infectious disease outbreak.
sentences.zh: 而现在，人们甚至在感冒时也会随手戴上口罩。

sentences.en: And now it's to the point where people will just wear them when they've got a cold.
sentences.zh: 这在这里已经很正常了。

sentences.en: It's just normal here.
sentences.zh: 她说，至少戴口罩并不是一件奇怪的事。

sentences.en: She said at least wearing a mask is not strange.
sentences.zh: 冬天戴是为了保暖，或者防范污染，又或者你感冒了，都可以戴。

sentences.en: You wear it in the winter to keep warm or to protect from pollution or if you have a cold.
sentences.zh: 这是一种常态化的日常行为。

sentences.en: It's a normalized daily behavior.
sentences.zh: 而且没有人会因为你选择戴口罩而用异样的眼光看你。

sentences.en: And no one would look at you strangely for choosing to wear one.
sentences.zh: 是的，这在美国真的不是这样。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that really wasn't the case here in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在这一切发生之前如果你戴着口罩，人们会觉得莫名其妙。

sentences.en: I mean, if you were wearing a mask before all this, like, people would wonder why.
sentences.zh: 好在过去这几个星期里，这种情况似乎真的开始改变了。

sentences.en: It seems like that's really starting to change in the past couple weeks.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，现在我要说，商店里甚至走在街上的人里，大概有80%都戴着口罩。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, now I would say that maybe like 80% of the people in stores are wearing masks and even walking along the street.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于街上戴口罩这事，在湾区，我们其实有点佩戴N95口罩的历史，因为这里每年都有野火。

sentences.en: I mean, the street thing is that in the Bay Area, we actually have a little bit of a history of wearing N95 masks because there's wildfires here every year.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于戴口罩这事，在湾区其实我们一直有点戴N95口罩的历史，因为这里每年都会发生山火。

sentences.en: And so it's not uncommon for people to have a couple in their home to deal with smoke.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们家里备着几个应对烟雾的面罩是很常见的。

sentences.en: So I think we were more ready to take on masks, but I've never seen them like this.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我们更准备好戴口罩了，但我从没见过这样的口罩。

sentences.en: I mean, it's totally like people are wearing every type of thing, homemade masks, N95 masks.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，完全就像每个人都在戴各种各样的东西，自制口罩、N95口罩。

sentences.en: They're really everywhere.
sentences.zh: 它们真的无处不在。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that's quite different from the past because I've been hearing from Asian American friends that there was like real trepidation about wearing a mask in public.
sentences.zh: 是的，这和过去有很大不同，因为我听亚裔美国人朋友说，在公共场合戴口罩真的让人非常忐忑。

sentences.en: Because the culture of masks is so different or has been so different in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因为美国的口罩文化太不一样了，或者说一直以来都很不一样。

sentences.en: And there was a lot of fear about how they would be perceived wearing a mask.
sentences.zh: 而且人们非常担心戴口罩会被别人怎么看。

sentences.en: And Professor Linteris talked about this.
sentences.zh: 林特里斯教授谈到了这一点。

sentences.en: The masks have become very aggressively and viciously racialized, right?
sentences.zh: 口罩已经被非常激进且恶毒地打上了种族标签，对吧？

sentences.en: They're associated with China, with Chinese people in a very xenophobic manner.
sentences.zh: 它们以一种非常排外的形式与中国、中国人民联系在一起。

sentences.en: So xenophobia is basically racism towards ethnically Chinese people.
sentences.zh: 所以仇外心理基本上就是针对华裔的种族主义。

sentences.en: And so you have this phenomenon which some journalists call maskophobia, which is basically an attribute of xenophobia.
sentences.zh: 因此你会发现这种现象，一些记者称之为“恐戴口罩症”，这基本上是仇外心理的一种表现。

sentences.en: People being attacked, like people who look Chinese or who look Asian, being attacked on the streets of London and other places because they're wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 人们遭到袭击，比如那些看起来像中国或亚洲面孔的人，在伦敦和其他地方的街头遭到袭击，因为他们戴着口罩。

sentences.en: Professor Linteris says this kind of insidious racism isn't even recognized by most people, but it's always been connected with disease.
sentences.zh: 林特里斯教授说，这种潜移默化的种族主义甚至没有被大多数人意识到，但它一直与疾病联系在一起。

sentences.en: So from the very birth of xenophobia in modern Europe and America, xenophobia has been connected with this idea of epidemics coming from China and being spread by Chinese people,
sentences.zh: 所以从现代欧美仇外心理诞生之初，仇外心理就与中国爆发并由中国人民传播的流行病这种观念联系在一起，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And I think that the mask and maskophobia is kind of, is tied to these racist and xenophobic attitudes.
sentences.zh: 我认为口罩和恐戴口罩症在某种程度上与这些种族主义和仇外态度挂钩。

sentences.en: But in China, there's no maskophobia.
sentences.zh: 但在中国，没有恐戴口罩症。

sentences.en: It's people who aren't wearing masks during this pandemic that are seen as strange.
sentences.zh: 在这场大流行期间，反而是那些不戴口罩的人被视为奇怪。

sentences.en: It is, you know, the baseline, as it were, of self-protection.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这可以说是自我保护的底线。

sentences.en: But more importantly, more, it's not so much about protecting yourself against being infected.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，与其说是为了保护自己免受感染，

sentences.en: It is more of protecting others.
sentences.zh: 不如说是为了保护他人。

sentences.en: I think this is something I didn't really fully appreciate at the beginning of all this.
sentences.zh: 我想这是我在这一切刚开始时并没有真正完全体会到的一点。

sentences.en: I mean, I think I had this instinct that when people were wearing masks before, that they were trying to protect themselves.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想我有一种直觉，以前人们戴口罩时，是想保护自己。

sentences.en: They were really worried about their own health when it came to a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 当涉及大流行时，他们真的很担心自己的健康。

sentences.en: But the truth is, it's like the opposite of that.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，这恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Like they have a little bit of cold and they don't want to spread it to you.
sentences.zh: 比如他们有点感冒，不想传染给你。

sentences.en: You know, a mask does a really good job of keeping them from spreading it to you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，口罩在阻止他们把病毒传染给你这件事上做得很棒。

sentences.en: They're protecting me.
sentences.zh: 他们在保护我。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They're being conscientious.
sentences.zh: 他们很有心。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, have you gotten used to wearing a mask regularly?
sentences.zh: 那么，你习惯经常戴口罩了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it's definitely not fun to wear a mask.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，戴口罩绝对谈不上有趣。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm not going to lie.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我不会撒谎。

sentences.en: I mean, I have glasses.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我戴眼镜。

sentences.en: Wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 戴着口罩。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, that's the worSt.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，那是糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: Oh, it's the worSt.
sentences.zh: 哦，真是糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's tough.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很难熬。

sentences.en: They made me feel really depressed.
sentences.zh: 它们让我感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: But during this outbreak, I'm really surprised.
sentences.zh: 但在这场疫情期间，我真的很惊讶。

sentences.en: They do not make me feel depressed.
sentences.zh: 它们并没有让我感到沮丧。

sentences.en: And I feel like seeing everyone around me wearing a mask, I feel like a sense of solidarity.
sentences.zh: 我觉得看到周围每个人都戴着口罩，我有一种团结感。

sentences.en: I mean, I can't see their face.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我看不到他们的脸。

sentences.en: I can't see their whole face.
sentences.zh: 我看不到他们的全脸。

sentences.en: But I feel like we're telling each other, I'm watching out for you.
sentences.zh: 但我感觉我们在告诉彼此，我在守护你。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And, I mean, I'm paying much more attention to people's eyes.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，我更加关注人们的眼睛了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because that's how I can tell what their expression is.
sentences.zh: 因为那样我才能看出他们的表情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You can see that they're smiling.
sentences.zh: 你能看出他们在笑。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, when I see other people wearing a mask, I feel like it's a reminder that we're all in this together.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，当我看到其他人戴着口罩时，我觉得这是一个提醒，提醒我们同舟共济。

sentences.en: Coming up, individual people are not the only ones changing their habits to deal with coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 接下来，改变习惯以应对冠状病毒的不止是个人。

sentences.en: Manufacturers are also finding themselves in uncharted waters, switching to produce the masks and gowns and ventilators that we need so desperately.
sentences.zh: 制造商们也发现自己身处未知的领域，转产我们迫切需要的口罩、防护服和呼吸机。

sentences.en: Some stories of the great manufacturing pivot of 2020.
sentences.zh: 一些关于2020年伟大制造业转型的故事。

sentences.en: After this.
sentences.zh: 广告之后继续。

sentences.en: About three weeks ago, Tyler Mantel was in a Home Depot at 6 a.m.
sentences.zh: 大约三周前，泰勒·曼特尔早上6点出现在一家家得宝商店。

sentences.en: Taking his first steps in trying to solve a huge global problem.
sentences.zh: 迈出了试图解决一个巨大的全球问题的第一步。

sentences.en: Just looking at just a wall of parts and pieces and hoses, just trying to figure out what I could put together to put together a baseline ventilator.
sentences.zh: 只是看着一整面墙的零件、组件和软管，努力弄清楚我可以把什么拼凑在一起，做出一个基础呼吸机。

sentences.en: A mechanical ventilator that could assist someone who has trouble breathing because they have COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 一个可以辅助因感染新冠肺炎而呼吸困难的人的机械呼吸机。

sentences.en: And anytime you're starting a design process, you need something.
sentences.zh: 任何时候，当你开始设计流程时，你都需要点东西。

sentences.en: As you're communicating with teams, the first thing you put together allows people to understand direction and it defines things you never thought you'd define.
sentences.zh: 当你与团队沟通时，你拼凑出的第一样东西能让大家理解方向，并定义那些你从未想过要定义的东西。

sentences.en: So just having a physical construct can always be very helpful.
sentences.zh: 所以仅仅拥有一个实体结构总是非常有帮助的。

sentences.en: So Tyler and his colleagues are in the Home Depot and none of the stuff on the wall is designed for ventilators.
sentences.zh: 因此，泰勒和他的同事们在家得宝，而墙上的所有东西都不是为呼吸机设计的。

sentences.en: Staring at a wall of one-way valves for PET connections.
sentences.zh: 盯着一整面用于PET连接的单向阀墙。

sentences.en: Like, they didn't fit onto what we were using at all.
sentences.zh: 就像是，它们根本不适合我们当时用的东西。

sentences.en: They were silly, but they, and they were the wrong pressure grade.
sentences.zh: 它们很荒谬，而且它们的压力等级不对。

sentences.en: Everything was wrong about it.
sentences.zh: 关于它的一切都是错的。

sentences.en: But we needed to understand what it is we were working with.
sentences.zh: 但我们需要了解我们正在处理的是什么。

sentences.en: It was interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: It was a throwback to the scene in Apollo 13.
sentences.zh: 这让人想起《阿波罗13号》里的那一幕。

sentences.en: This is the scene where the mission control technicians have to figure out how to fit a square filter into a round hole
sentences.zh: 这是任务控制中心的技师们必须想办法把一个方形过滤器塞进圆形孔洞的场景

sentences.en: using only the items that can be found in the Apollo 13 spacecraft, or all the astronauts are going to die.
sentences.zh: 只能使用在阿波罗13号飞船上能找到的物品，否则所有宇航员都会死。

sentences.en: Okay, people, listen up.
sentences.zh: 好了，各位，听着。

sentences.en: People upstairs, hand it us this one, and we gotta come through.
sentences.zh: 楼上的人把这个交给了我们，我们必须成功。

sentences.en: We gotta find a way to make this fit into the hole for this, using nothing but that.
sentences.zh: 我们必须找到一种方法，只用那个东西，把它塞进这个洞里。

sentences.en: Damn, that's the greatest scene in movie history.
sentences.zh: 该死，那是电影史上最棒的一幕。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样。

sentences.en: We just started throwing stuff in a cart.
sentences.zh: 我们只是开始把东西往购物车里扔。

sentences.en: I think I put $150, $200 on my credit card and ran a bunch of stuff to the lab,
sentences.zh: 我想我在信用卡上刷了150、200美元，把一堆东西拿回了实验室，

sentences.en: and we started piling things together until it made our first iteration of a ventilator.
sentences.zh: 然后我们开始把东西堆在一起，直到做出了我们的第一代呼吸机原型。

sentences.en: As you can tell, Tyler Mantel doesn't normally make ventilators.
sentences.zh: 正如你所看到的，泰勒·曼特尔通常不制造呼吸机。

sentences.en: So most of the time, I make robots that swim through water pipes to find leaks.
sentences.zh: 所以大多数时候，我制造在水管中游动以寻找泄漏的机器人。

sentences.en: This is a huge problem with old infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 这是老旧基础设施的一个巨大问题。

sentences.en: 20% of the world's clean water is lost to leaky pipes.
sentences.zh: 世界上20%的清洁水都因管道泄漏而损失了。

sentences.en: But suddenly, that wasn't the most pressing problem in the world.
sentences.zh: 但突然之间，这不再是世界上最紧迫的问题了。

sentences.en: When coronavirus came and hit us like it did,
sentences.zh: 当冠状病毒到来并像那样冲击我们时，

sentences.en: the ability to travel and do some of the big projects we have coming up went away.
sentences.zh: 出行的能力以及我们即将开展的一些大项目都泡汤了。

sentences.en: So we started to look at what else we could do.
sentences.zh: 所以我们开始寻找我们还能做些什么。

sentences.en: And my co-founder of the Ventilator Project is actually also my roommate.
sentences.zh: 呼吸机项目的联合创始人实际上也是我的室友。

sentences.en: We work in the same building,
sentences.zh: 我们在同一栋楼工作，

sentences.en: and we just started talking about the fact that ventilators are going to be a huge shortage.
sentences.zh: 我们开始讨论呼吸机将严重短缺这一事实。

sentences.en: And so I started digging into it,
sentences.zh: 于是我开始深入研究，

sentences.en: and you start to find out that a ventilator is not a difficult product.
sentences.zh: 你开始发现呼吸机并不是一个复杂的的产品。

sentences.en: The lack of difficulty doesn't mean it's easy.
sentences.zh: 不复杂并不意味着它很简单。

sentences.en: It means it's straightforward.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它很直接明了。

sentences.en: So Tyler and his co-founder at the Ventilator Project, Alex Frost,
sentences.zh: 因此，泰勒和他在呼吸机项目的联合创始人亚历克斯·弗罗斯特，

sentences.en: assembled a team of over 200 remote volunteer engineers, medical, regulatory, and business professionals
sentences.zh: 组建了一支由200多名远程志愿者工程师、医疗、监管和商业专业人士组成的团队，

sentences.en: to try and help solve the global ventilator shortage as fast as possible.
sentences.zh: 试图以最快速度帮助解决全球呼吸机短缺问题。

sentences.en: And even though the details from company to company are very different,
sentences.zh: 尽管每家公司的细节大不相同，

sentences.en: a lot of manufacturers are making a similar pivot.
sentences.zh: 但许多制造商都在进行类似的转型。

sentences.en: You know, if you're a manufacturer, that's kind of what you're always looking like.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你是一个制造商，这基本上就是你一直在寻找的。

sentences.en: Can we make something like that?
sentences.zh: 我们能做那样东西吗？

sentences.en: Can we make that?
sentences.zh: 我们能做那个吗？

sentences.en: That's sort of in our blood, you know?
sentences.zh: 这有点刻在我们的骨子里，你知道吗？

sentences.en: This is Matt Anderson, the co-founder of Sound Devices.
sentences.zh: 这是马特·安德森，Sound Devices的联合创始人。

sentences.en: They normally make high-end audio mixing and recording consoles.
sentences.zh: 他们通常制造高端音频混音和录音控制台。

sentences.en: A couple weeks ago, I was texting back and forth with my head of manufacturing, Lisa,
sentences.zh: 几周前，我和我的制造主管丽莎发短信，

sentences.en: and said, you know, I wonder if we could make ventilators or masks or something.
sentences.zh: 说，你知道的，我在想我们能不能制造呼吸机、口罩什么的。

sentences.en: They ended up concentrating on face shield masks.
sentences.zh: 他们最终专注于防护面罩。

sentences.en: I came in and talked to my sales guys and said, hey, do you guys want to call some hospitals
sentences.zh: 我走进去跟我的销售人员说，嘿，你们想不想给一些医院打电话，

sentences.en: and see if this is true about there being a shortage?
sentences.zh: 看看短缺这事是不是真的？

sentences.en: Because I don't know.
sentences.zh: 因为我不知道。

sentences.en: And they made some calls and they came back and they said, yeah, definitely hospitals really need these badly.
sentences.zh: 然后他们打了几个电话回来后说，是的，确实，医院非常急需这些。

sentences.en: So that's, you know, a few minutes later, we just started buying parts.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，几分钟后，我们就开始购买零件了。

sentences.en: You know, that was on a Monday that we started that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们是周一开始这么做的。

sentences.en: And then it was 32 hours later, we had the first ones coming off the end of the line.
sentences.zh: 32小时后，第一批产品就从生产线上下来了。

sentences.en: And today, if you go to the product page on sounddevices.com, you can order a 32-channel,
sentences.zh: 今天，如果你去 sounddevices.com 的产品页面，你可以订购一个32通道、

sentences.en: 36-track mixer and a 100-pack of single-use medical face shields.
sentences.zh: 36轨的混音器以及一包100个的一次性医疗防护面罩。

sentences.en: And much like the ventilator project, when Matt described his company's pivot to our producer,
sentences.zh: 和呼吸机项目很像，当马特向我们的制片人埃米特·菲茨杰拉德——你将在下一段听到他的声音——描述他公司的转型时，并不是制造产品所需的技术或专业知识。

sentences.en: Emmett Fitzgerald, who you'll hear in the next clip, it wasn't the technology or the know-how needed to make the product.
sentences.zh: 那才是困难的部分。

sentences.en: That was the hard part.
sentences.zh: 你拿海绵，粘在上面，把松紧带订上去，就完成了。

sentences.en: You take the foam, stick it on there, staple on the elastic and you're done.
sentences.zh: 听起来真的很简单。

sentences.en: It sounds really simple.
sentences.zh: 但要大批量获得这三个零件一直很困难。

sentences.en: But getting these three parts in volume has been difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有供应商，这是我们塑料面罩和海绵的常规供应商。

sentences.en: So we have supplier, it's our normal suppliers for the plastic shield and for the foam.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，我们有很好的供应商提供这些。

sentences.en: Luckily, we've got great suppliers for them.
sentences.zh: 他们就在威斯康星州附近，我们买它们的材料，一切都很好。

sentences.en: They're right nearby in Wisconsin and we buy them and that's all great.
sentences.zh: 松紧带这部分，要大量搞到简直是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: The elastic piece, that's been kind of a nightmare to get in quantity.
sentences.zh: 我举个例子，上周，我们的两名采购人员洛林和陈怡，

sentences.en: I'll give you a, for instance, last week, two of our purchasing people, Lorraine and Chen Yee,
sentences.zh: 开车跑遍了威斯康星州北部，从一家沃尔玛到另一家沃尔玛，从一家乔安面料店到另一家乔安面料店，

sentences.en: were driving all around northern Wisconsin, going from Walmart to Walmart and Joanne's Fabric to Joanne's Fabric,
sentences.zh: 买光了他们能找到的所有松紧带。

sentences.en: buying up all the elastic they could find.
sentences.zh: 我觉得当你想象制造业时，你不会想象制造商开车去乔安面料店买他们制造产品用的材料。

sentences.en: I feel like when you picture manufacturing, you don't picture manufacturers driving to Joanne Fabrics to get the stuff they're making.
sentences.zh: 嗯，通常你不会，但这是一个特殊情况，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, and normally you don't, but this is a special situation, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 通常你打电话时，你会说，我想买这么多海绵。

sentences.en: It's typical when you call, you say, I want to buy this much foam.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，交货时间是六周。

sentences.en: And they say, the lead time is six weeks.
sentences.zh: 然后你说，好的，没问题。

sentences.en: And you go, okay, no problem.
sentences.zh: 你为此做计划。

sentences.en: You plan for that.
sentences.zh: 但在这次大流行中，六周对我们一点帮助都没有。

sentences.en: Well, in this pandemic, six weeks does us no good.
sentences.zh: 供应链、规章制度和工厂必须比以往任何时候都更加灵活，因为病毒是一个移动的目标。

sentences.en: Supply chains, regulations, and factories have to be more nimble than ever before because the virus is a moving target.
sentences.zh: 问问底特律工业缝纫与创新中心首席执行官詹·加里诺就知道了，他们通常制作时尚服装。

sentences.en: Just ask Jen Garino, CEO of the Industrial Sewing and Innovation Center in Detroit, which normally makes fashion apparel.
sentences.zh: 我必须告诉你，这是一个变化如此之快的环境。

sentences.en: I will tell you that this has been such a quickly changing environment.
sentences.zh: 起初，全是口罩、口罩、口罩、口罩。

sentences.en: At first, it was mass, mass, mass, mass.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们制作了所有这些口罩、所有这些口罩的样品。

sentences.en: So, we sampled all these mass, all these mass.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们制作了所有这些口罩、所有这些口罩的样品。

sentences.en: And then it was no longer mass.
sentences.zh: 然后它就不再是大众产品了。

sentences.en: It was really gowns.
sentences.zh: 而实际上是医用手术衣。

sentences.en: And gowns has really turned out to be the big problem and really what we're most suited to make.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，医用手术衣成了最大的难题，也确实是我们最擅长制造的东西。

sentences.en: And what is an isolation gown exactly?
sentences.zh: 那么，到底什么是隔离衣呢？

sentences.en: So, an isolation gown is, there's varying degrees.
sentences.zh: 所以，隔离衣是有不同等级的。

sentences.en: And trust me, when I say I have learned a lot in the last three weeks, I have, wow.
sentences.zh: 相信我，过去三周我学到了很多东西，真的，哇。

sentences.en: I mean, acronyms I didn't know before, the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，各种以前不知道的缩写词，还有整套流程。

sentences.en: What makes an isolation gown is that it has particulate protection to varying degrees.
sentences.zh: 隔离衣之所以成为隔离衣，是因为它具有不同程度的颗粒物防护功能。

sentences.en: So, if you're in surgery, you have, you know, really tight cuffs around your wrist and tight around your neck and your highest grade material.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你在做手术，你知道的，手腕上有很紧的袖口，脖子周围也很紧，并且采用最高等级的材料。

sentences.en: And a level one, it's just sort of like a sheet that you put over that just, you know, helps you a little bit.
sentences.zh: 至于一级隔离衣，它有点像你套在外面的一张薄板，你知道的，能起到一点防护作用。

sentences.en: The Industrial Sewing and Innovation Center, also known as ISAC, was already a mission-driven company before coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 工业缝纫与创新中心，也被称为ISAC，在冠状病毒爆发之前就已经是 一家有使命感的公司了。

sentences.en: So, the Industrial Sewing and Innovation Center is designed to be a people-centered institute that trains people for advanced manufacturing of sewn goods like apparel.
sentences.zh: 所以，工业缝纫与创新中心的宗旨是建立一个以人为本的机构，培训人们从事服装等缝制商品的先进制造。

sentences.en: And to do so in a way that is responsible.
sentences.zh: 并且以一种负责任的方式来做到这一点。

sentences.en: The fashion industry is a very polluting, irresponsible industry for the most part.
sentences.zh: 对大多数情况而言，时尚产业是一个污染严重、极不负责任的行业。

sentences.en: It puts about 45 billion units of garments into landfills every year before a consumer.
sentences.zh: 它每年在消费者购买之前，就会将大约 450 亿件服装投入垃圾填埋场。

sentences.en: One of the solutions to changing these bad practices is to manufacture closer to home.
sentences.zh: 改变这些不良做法的解决方案之一，就是在更靠近本土的地方进行制造。

sentences.en: So, instead of stores speculatively buying clothes they think will sell nine months in the future,
sentences.zh: 因此，商店不再凭猜测购买他们认为能在九个月后售出的服装，

sentences.en: they use more advanced and local manufacturing to quickly fulfill orders on demand.
sentences.zh: 而是利用更先进的本地制造来按需快速完成订单。

sentences.en: So, you get rid of a whole waste stream and now you have a whole resource pool that you can now allocate to paying higher wages.
sentences.zh: 这样，你就消除了整个废物流，现在你有了一个完整的资源池，你可以将其分配用于支付更高的工资。

sentences.en: And being sustainable from that standpoint, we really believe that having a sustainable product is not sustainable unless the people making them have sustainable lives.
sentences.zh: 从这个角度来看，要保持可持续发展，我们坚信，除非制造产品的人们拥有可持续的生活，否则拥有可持续的产品是不可持续的。

sentences.en: You can't fight every battle at the same time.
sentences.zh: 你不可能同时打赢每一场仗。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I totally get that.
sentences.zh: 我完全理解这一点。

sentences.en: But how have you approached balancing your mission to the moment?
sentences.zh: 但是，你是如何平衡当下的使命的呢？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You can't make everything first priority.
sentences.zh: 你不能把所有事情都当作第一优先级。

sentences.en: So, sustainability, I will have to tell you right now, is not our number one, you know, priority because, I mean, we're working on polypropylene.
sentences.zh: 所以，我必须现在就告诉你，可持续发展并不是我们的头号优先级，你知道的，因为，我的意思是，我们正在使用聚丙烯。

sentences.en: And these are disposable gowns.
sentences.zh: 这些都是一次性隔离衣。

sentences.en: You wear them once and you throw them out.
sentences.zh: 你穿一次就扔掉了。

sentences.en: It's the opposite of sustainable.
sentences.zh: 这完全是可持续的对立面。

sentences.en: You know?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: But, you know, we have learned.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我们已经学到了很多。

sentences.en: We've learned a lot about how that stuff gets recycled.
sentences.zh: 我们学到了很多关于这些东西是如何被回收利用的知识。

sentences.en: So, you know, we're learning as we go about these waste streams and what you can do about these waste streaMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，我们在边做边学，了解这些废物流以及你能对这些废物流做些什么。

sentences.en: So, it's interesting that even though we're creating more ways, we're also understanding what you do with it when it's done.
sentences.zh: 所以，有趣的是，尽管我们制造了更多的垃圾，但我们也开始明白当它们废弃时该如何处理。

sentences.en: But I think what hasn't changed is our commitment to training people and treating people differently than they've been treated in a factory environment.
sentences.zh: 但我认为没有改变的是我们培训员工的承诺，以及以不同于工厂环境的方式对待员工。

sentences.en: So, we're just making different products.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们只是在制造不同的产品。

sentences.en: So, how do you physically make the factory safe so that workers can be separate and still do their jobs?
sentences.zh: 那么，你如何在物理上让工厂变得安全，以便工人们可以保持距离又能完成他们的工作呢？

sentences.en: Ah, good question.
sentences.zh: 啊，好问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, one of the things that we had to do is when you're manufacturing in a lean way, you reduce costs by reducing the space by which you hand things to each other.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们必须做的一件事是，当你在进行精益制造时，你是通过减少传递物品之间的空间来降低成本的。

sentences.en: So, in a typical cell...
sentences.zh: 所以，在一个典型的生产单元里……

sentences.en: A cell is a team of people working on different parts of an item.
sentences.zh: 一个生产单元是一组致力于制作物品不同部件的人。

sentences.en: Once the item's through the cell, it's completed.
sentences.zh: 一旦物品通过了这个单元，它就完成了。

sentences.en: Literally, you have pieces of fabric that are tied together that are kind of making their way around, you know, the cell.
sentences.zh: 字面意思上，你会看到一捆捆绑在一起的面料，在生产单元里流转。

sentences.en: So, you're very, very, very close and that's how you remain competitive.
sentences.zh: 所以，你们挨得非常非常近，这就是你们保持竞争力的方式。

sentences.en: So, we had to distance that.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们必须拉开距离。

sentences.en: So, literally, what we did was we have these brand new gorgeous machines that, you know, they're programmable.
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上，我们做的是拥有这些全新的、华丽的机器，你知道的，它们是可编程的。

sentences.en: They're really beautiful.
sentences.zh: 它们真的很漂亮。

sentences.en: And in between them, we've rigged these, you know, corrugated cardboard pathways, sort of duct taped, you know, between machines so that we can create enough distance,
sentences.zh: 在它们之间，我们用胶带固定了这些瓦楞纸板通道，你知道的，连接在机器之间，这样我们就能拉开足够的距离，

sentences.en: at least six feet, to pass the, you know, material cross and then to wear masks and the gloves.
sentences.zh: 至少六英尺，以便把材料递过去，然后戴上口罩和手套。

sentences.en: So, it's been this real, you know, just figure it out, make it work.
sentences.zh: 所以，这真的是那种摸着石头过河、设法让它运转的过程。

sentences.en: As we continue to navigate the pandemic, notably without the proper planning and guidance from our federal executive,
sentences.zh: 在我们继续应对这场大流行病的过程中，尤其是缺乏联邦行政部门的适当规划和指导时，

sentences.en: relying on the ingenuity and generosity of these manufacturers to fill in the gaps.
sentences.zh: 我们只能依靠这些制造商的独创性和慷慨解囊来填补空缺。

sentences.en: There will be a lot of just figuring it out.
sentences.zh: 会有很多见招拆招、摸索前进的情况。
